**(Before the lights, before the roar, there is just _this_. The air itself feels heavy here. Thick with the ghosts of industry, the mineral tang of coal dust that never quite washes away from the back of the throat, the damp, pervasive chill rising off the slag heaps and the slow, grey river choking on its own sediment. This is the Belt. Rust, not merely as color, but as _condition_. A landscape etched in corrosion, where brick facades weep mortar like old wounds and skeletal frameworks of forgotten factories claw at an indifferent sky - monuments to a promise that packed up and left town decades ago, leaving behind a silence thick with unspoken loss.)**

Resilience, though... resilience is different. It's in the stubborn weeds forcing through pavement cracks, in the flickering neon sign of a 24-hour diner defying the gloom like a battered prizefighter, in the tired eyes of people who learned long ago that getting knocked down wasn't an option, just an _intermission_ before the next round. It's a hard, unlovely thing, this endurance, ground into the very bone of the place.)**

**(This is the world that breathes you, Iron Maiden. Its decay is mirrored in the chill that sometimes seeps into your joints, its flashes of defiant fire reflected in the embers banked behind your eyes, its suffocating weight echoed in the pressure that constricts your chest when the walls close in.
